name: Ernesto And Fabio Bertarelli
current_role: Ernesto Bertarelli: head of B-FLEXION (formerly Waypoint Capital), Geneva; co-chair, Bertarelli Foundation
profile: 1997 Forbes entry for father and son behind Swiss biotech Serono. Fabio Bertarelli died in 1998; son Ernesto (b. 1965) ran Serono from 1996, shifted it to biotech and sold it to Merck KGaA in 2007 for $13.3bn. He now invests the family fortune via B-FLEXION and co-chairs the Bertarelli Foundation with sister Dona.
interesting_fact: Ernesto founded sailing team Alinghi, which won the America's Cup in 2003 on its first attempt, bringing the Cup to Europe for the first time; he was the team's only Swiss national, serving as navigator.
deep_cut_fact: The name Alinghi comes from the Bertarelli family boats that raced around Porto Santo Stefano and Porto Ercole on Monte Argentario, where Ernesto spent his youth sailing.
notes: Fabio Bertarelli (the father) died in 1998, so alive=unknown covers the pair: Ernesto is alive, Fabio is not. Profile focuses on Ernesto. The family site lists no published email. Best route is probably B-FLEXION in Geneva or the Bertarelli Foundation, whose marine-conservation work has protected over 3m km2 of ocean since 2010.

name: Vince McMahon
current_role: Founder of 14TH & I, a private sports, media and entertainment investment firm (Connecticut)
profile: Former WWE chairman and CEO. He bought his father's wrestling company in 1982 and built WWE into a global media business, which merged with UFC to form TKO in 2023. He resigned from TKO in January 2024 and in 2025 launched 14TH & I, named for the D.C. intersection where his father's Capitol Wrestling Corp. was based.
interesting_fact: McMahon was behind the 1976 Muhammad Ali vs. Antonio Inoki match, years before he took over his father's promotion.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from East Carolina University in 1968 and working as a traveling salesman, he became a ring announcer in 1969. In 1971 he promoted his first card, in a small territory in Maine.
notes: Sensitive: he resigned from TKO in January 2024 amid a lawsuit alleging sexual misconduct, and in January 2025 he settled SEC charges over undisclosed payments (>$1.7m). Weigh reputational fit before any outreach. 14TH & I's site published no contact details; reported executives are Brad Blum (president) and David Spingarn (CIO), per https://wrestletalk.com/news/vince-mcmahon-new-company-wwe-exit-revealed/

name: Prakash Parmanand Hinduja
current_role: Chairman, Hinduja Group (Europe); Chairman of the Advisory Board, Hinduja Bank (Switzerland)
profile: Prakash 'PP' Hinduja is the third of the four Hinduja brothers behind the Hinduja Group, a conglomerate whose interests span Ashok Leyland, IndusInd Bank, Gulf Oil, energy and media. He ran the group's European operations from Geneva and has been based in Monaco since 2008. After brother Gopichand's death in November 2025, he and Ashok are the surviving brothers of that generation.
interesting_fact: He and his brothers built the group, founded by their father P.D. Hinduja, into an international conglomerate with a footprint across about 38 countries and a 200,000-plus workforce.
deep_cut_fact: After university, PP began in the family business in Tehran, Iran, before moving to Geneva to take charge of the group's European operations. He also sits on the board of the Swiss-Indian Chamber of Commerce.
notes: Born 1945. Sensitive: in 2024 a Geneva court convicted Prakash and family members in a case over the treatment of domestic staff; check the current status before outreach. The group's Energy/Hinduja Renewables arm (multi-GW generation plans in India) fits the podcast's energy angle. Group contact page lists business-unit emails but none for him personally.
